clue.text: Err like inactive partner when rise is delayed?

definitions.text: Err like inactive partner when rise is delayed?

parts.words: Err like inactive partner when rise is delayed?
parts.note: a sleeping partner takes no active part; to go wrong by sleeping too much, so that getting up comes late

explanation.surface: A business partner who does nothing makes a mistake by getting up late.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'sleeping partner' is a British term for an investor who takes no part in running the business; the clue imagines one going wrong by sleeping too long.
explanation.definitionFit: Staying in bed past the intended waking time is exactly a delayed rising.

clue.text: Antiquated honour only Tories originally received

indicators.note: the honour takes in the words that follow, so they sit inside it

parts.note: OBE, Officer of the Order of the British Empire, is a British honour
sole means only

indicators.note: originally picks the first letter of Tories

explanation.surface: An outdated award that was given only to Conservatives at first.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe something out of date and no longer in use.

clue.text: No time for intimidation-it's not right

indicators.note: no time means the letter for time is dropped from the word for intimidation

parts.note: terror is the fear that intimidation produces

explanation.surface: A protest that bullying is wrong and there is no time for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A mistake is something incorrect, a thing that is wrong.

clue.text: To wit, it calls up a branch of linguistics

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the whole run is read from bottom to top

parts.note: SC is short for scilicet, Latin for namely, to wit
to name is to call

explanation.surface: A remark that 'to wit' summons up a field of language study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Calls up' looks like summoning; 'up' alone is the reversal and turns all three pieces, giving SEMAN, TI and CS.
explanation.definitionFit: This field studies meaning in language, one division of the science of language.

clue.text: Working at ropes, possibly made from this

definitions.text: Working at ropes, possibly made from this

indicators.note: working means the letters of at ropes are set in motion into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone at work on ropes that might be woven from this material.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: ropes may be made from this grass, and its letters are those of AT ROPES.
explanation.definitionFit: Esparto is a tough Spanish grass whose fibres are made into rope, mats and paper.

clue.text: Select a vulgar sounding player

indicators.note: sounding means the words are spoken, and their sound gives the answer

parts.note: pick (select) a low (vulgar), spoken together

explanation.surface: Choose a coarse-sounding musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Select a vulgar' gives PICK A LOW, which said aloud gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word can mean the instrument or, in an orchestra, the person who plays it.

clue.text: For a bird, this is just what's needed with seed

parts.note: a pip is the seed of a fruit such as an apple
'it' as in 'that's it', exactly the thing required

explanation.surface: A bird-feeding tip: seed is precisely the thing to offer.
explanation.definitionFit: The meadow pipit and tree pipit are small brown songbirds.

clue.text: Worthing nurse's solid figure

definitions.meaning: Miss ..., governess in Wilde's The Importance of Being Earnest, who as a nursemaid lost the infant Jack Worthing
a solid with two identical parallel ends joined by flat sides

explanation.definitionFit: Wilde named the nursemaid after the geometric solid; both senses carry the same name.

clue.text: Involved in a task accepted by pious countryman

indicators.note: the anagram is taken inside the word for pious

parts.note: pi is informal British shorthand for pious

indicators.note: involved means tangled, so the letters of in a task are mixed up

explanation.surface: A devout farmer gets caught up in a job.
explanation.definitionFit: Countryman here means compatriot, a native of a given country.

clue.text: Drive horse in confident expectation

indicators.note: the horse letter is placed inside the expectation word

parts.note: trust is a firm belief in something
H is slang for heroin, which is also called horse

explanation.surface: Ride a horse with assurance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horse' is slang for heroin, whose abbreviation is H.
explanation.definitionFit: As nouns both mean forceful push or energy.

clue.text: Clear off when resistance disrupts criminal activity

indicators.note: the resistance letter breaks into the middle of the criminal scheme

parts.note: a scam is a fraudulent scheme
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Crooks flee when someone resists their racket.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal commands to go away at once.

clue.text: Outgoing consumer whose preparations may be hampered

definitions.text: Outgoing consumer whose preparations may be hampered

parts.words: Outgoing consumer whose preparations may be hampered
parts.note: an eater on an outing whose food is packed in a wicker basket, a hamper, rather than obstructed

explanation.surface: A sociable shopper finds their plans obstructed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hampered' seems to mean obstructed and 'outgoing' sociable; in fact the food is packed in a hamper for an outing.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone eating an outdoor meal on an excursion typically carries food in a wicker basket.

clue.text: Man who made a bit from soldiers on board ship

indicators.note: being on board means being inside the vessel, so the soldiers go within the ship

parts.note: a liner is a large passenger ship
OR stands for Other Ranks, soldiers who are not officers

explanation.surface: A man earned a little money from troops serving aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made a bit' looks like earning some money; the bit is the metal mouthpiece of a horse's bridle.
explanation.definitionFit: A loriner is a craftsman making bits, spurs and other metal fittings for horse harness.

clue.text: Gradual assimilation of one employed in very large plant

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize

indicators.note: the numeral is put to work inside the following words, so it goes within them

parts.note: moss is a small flowerless plant
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone works slowly into their job at a huge factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' suggests a factory and 'employed' a job; here the plant is moss and 'employed in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is used figuratively for absorbing ideas or knowledge steadily without conscious effort.

clue.text: Like the inexactitude of Churchill's speech

definitions.text: Like the inexactitude of Churchill's speech

parts.words: Like the inexactitude of Churchill's speech
parts.note: Churchill coined the euphemism '... inexactitude' for a lie in a 1906 Commons speech; the word wanted describes that inexactitude

explanation.surface: Commenting on an imprecise address by Churchill.
explanation.walkthrough: Churchill, avoiding the unparliamentary word 'lie', spoke of 'terminological inexactitude'; the clue asks for the first word of that phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to the choice of words, which is the kind of inexactitude Churchill named.

clue.text: Money received for off-the-peg garment

parts.note: the ready is British slang for cash
made means got or earned, as in made a profit

explanation.surface: Cash paid for a ready-to-wear outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: An item made in standard sizes and sold ready to wear, not tailored.

clue.text: Right to enter concert I organised? Not so

indicators.note: the letter for right goes into the anagram
organised means the letters of concert I are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Asking whether I was right to come into a concert I arranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is not so means it is false or wrong.

clue.text: Feelers of insect upset English girl

parts.note: an ant is an insect

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, read from bottom to top

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name

explanation.surface: An English girl is distressed by a bug's antennae.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' reverses E plus ANNE together, making ENNAE.
explanation.definitionFit: Insects' paired sensory organs on the head are called by this plural, which also serves as feelers.

clue.text: Palestrina's work? Turning out multiple copies

definitions.meaning: Palestrina, the Renaissance composer, wrote over a hundred settings of the Mass, so composing them was his trade
making identical items in large numbers by industrial process

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase normally means factory output in bulk, and punningly the writing of Masses.

clue.text: Respond when troop leaders enter, and withdraw

indicators.note: the leading letters go inside the word for respond

parts.note: to react is to respond

indicators.note: leaders picks the first letters of troop

explanation.surface: Reacting as the troop's officers come in, then pulling back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Troop leaders' gives T and R, the first two letters of troop.
explanation.definitionFit: To take back a statement, or to pull back in, is to draw it back.

clue.text: He takes steps to entertain, and sure gets into trouble

indicators.note: in trouble the letters of and and sure are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A performer goes to some lengths to amuse, and certainly lands in difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes steps' looks like taking measures; it means dance steps, and 'and' is part of the fodder, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A male ballet dancer entertains audiences with his steps.

clue.text: Protest in article

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means to raise a protest; as a noun it means a thing or item.

clue.text: Stab unknown individual in club

indicators.note: the unknown and the individual sit inside the club

parts.note: a bat is a club used in games
Y is an algebraic unknown
one is a single individual

explanation.surface: A stranger is knifed at a nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Club' suggests a nightclub; it is a bat.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to pierce with the blade fixed to a rifle.

clue.text: Welshman, turns up with an aquatic plant

indicators.note: in a down clue turns up means the run is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Dai is a typical Welsh man's name

explanation.surface: A Welshman arrives carrying a water plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turns up' looks like arrives, but it reverses DAI and AN together.
explanation.definitionFit: Naiad is a genus of submerged water plants, as well as a water nymph.

clue.text: Hurried back with speed to tell what happened

indicators.note: back means the word for hurried is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: ran is the past tense of run, hurried
rate means speed, as in a rate of knots

explanation.surface: A witness rushed back quickly to report an incident.
explanation.definitionFit: To recount events is to give a spoken or written account of them.

clue.text: Spontaneous comment from head librarian

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: The chief librarian makes an unscripted remark.
explanation.definitionFit: An improvised remark is made up on the spot, without preparation.

clue.text: Greek character detectives are about to remove

indicators.note: about here means turned round, applied to the whole run of three pieces

parts.note: eta is the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, British police detectives

explanation.surface: Police are poised to take away a Greek suspect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'on the point of', but it reverses ETA, CID and ARE together, giving ERA, DIC and ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To uproot or wipe out something completely is to get rid of it entirely.

clue.text: Lake lady initially taken in by extremely eligible knight

definitions.text: Lake lady initially taken in by extremely eligible knight

indicators.note: the two initials are received inside the outer letters that follow
extremely means take the first and last letters of eligible
initially picks the first letter of each of the two words before it

parts.note: N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: Scott's heroine is captured by a highly eligible knight.
explanation.walkthrough: Ellen Douglas is the heroine of Walter Scott's poem The Lady of the Lake, wooed by the knight James Fitz-James.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellen is the name of the heroine of Scott's poem, so she is the Lady of the Lake herself.

clue.text: Be inclined to cross river in this general direction

indicators.note: the inclined word is laid across the river letter, so that letter goes inside it

parts.note: to tend is to be inclined to do something
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Advice to wade a river heading roughly this way.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendency or drift is the overall course something takes.

clue.text: A supporter of revolutionary musical production

definitions.text: A supporter of revolutionary musical production

parts.words: A supporter of revolutionary musical production
parts.note: the rotating platform that holds up a spinning record while it plays

explanation.surface: A fan of a radical stage musical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolutionary musical production' suggests a politically radical show; it means music produced by a record going round.
explanation.definitionFit: On a record player the revolving deck holds the disc and turns it as it sounds.
